title: Arkansas cop tragically dies saving fiancée's life just hours after proposing
summary: An Arkansas police officer proposed to his fiancée hours before drowning in Elk River while rescuing her from the current during a canoeing trip with friends.
story: Josh Gill, United Cajun Navy Incident commander, and meteorologist Amy Metz provide firsthand accounts of dangerous Texas flood rescues, as two people have died. They emphasize improved preparedness compared to the previous year's tragic Camp Mystic floods, which killed 28. The Guadalupe River rose 32 feet in four hours, highlighting the need for vigilance.
An Arkansas police officer drowned after entering a river to save his fiancée just hours after proposing to her, according to her mother.

Fred Marsh, 24, of the Rogers Police Department, entered Missouri’s Elk River on Saturday to help another swimmer and did not resurface, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol. His fiancée’s mother identified that swimmer as her daughter. Marsh was recovered and pronounced dead Sunday after asking his fiancée, Hailey, to marry him Saturday morning.

"They had been together for three beautiful years, and they had a very beautiful, loving relationship," Sheryl Padgett told KHBS. "Even though legally he was not my son-in-law, he will forever be my son."

The pair, who had been together for three years, were out canoeing with another couple on the river near Noel, Missouri, when Hailey entered the water and began struggling against the current while trying to return to the boat.
‘HERO' MOM DIES AFTER USING LAST STRENGTH TO SAVE 4-YEAR-OLD SON FROM FLORIDA RIVER
Fred Marsh entered Elk River on Saturday and was recovered Sunday after asking his fiancée, Hailey, to marry him that morning. (GoFundMe)

Marsh and a fellow Rogers police officer who was with them then jumped into the water to help her, Padgett said. They were able to move her to safety, but Marsh became distressed and exhausted, went underwater and never resurfaced, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol.
"He saw the love of his life in distress, and he was going to help his friend and do what a good human would do," Padgett said. "He gave his life helping someone else."
Padgett said Marsh was loving, hardworking and guided by his Christian faith, emphasizing that he never hesitated when someone needed help.

"There’s nothing he wouldn’t do for anyone," Padgett said. "You didn’t have to tell him. You didn’t have to beg him. He just was willing and would jump in there and do whatever it took to help someone."
Padgett said she had lost her only son in a fatal accident four years earlier. She began calling Marsh her son soon after he started dating her daughter.
Fred Marsh and his fiancée, Hailey, had been together for three years. (GoFundMe)
"We instantly made a connection and a bond," she said. "I called him son, and he called me mama."

A motorcade escorted Marsh’s body through Northwest Arkansas on Monday as people lined up along the route to honor him. Padgett said the response from law enforcement and the community showed the impact Marsh had made on many others.
"They made it very clear that Fred was not just their family, but so was my daughter, my family and, even more importantly, Fred’s family," Padgett said.
Marsh was in his first year with the Rogers Police Department. He graduated from the Arkansas Law Enforcement Training Academy in April and only recently started working as an officer.
NYPD OFFICER SHOT, GUNMAN KILLED AFTER ARMED BARRICADED STANDOFF IN BROOKLYN: POLICE
Fred Marsh was in his first year with the Rogers Police Department. (GoFundMe)
A GoFundMe created for Hailey by her sister to cover her lease, bills and other unforeseen expenses has raised nearly $2,000 as of Thursday morning.
"Fred was an upstanding young man- Son, Fiancée, Officer, Brother, Friend, and more to all. We are devastated and will miss him dearly," the fundraiser reads.

Funeral arrangements are being handled by Marsh’s family, and Padgett said the family expects officers, former classmates, childhood friends and others from across the state to attend.
"Let’s do something in Fred’s honor," Padgett said. "Be kind to your fellow man. When Fred loved, he loved with everything he had, and he loved well."

title: Border K-9 sniffs out 99 pounds of prohibited meat, plants and monitor lizard in suitcase from Thailand
summary: K-9 Maisy discovered 50 pounds of raw meat, mangoes and 16 pounds of Bengal monitor lizard in luggage from Thailand, prompting a wildlife seizure.
story: Fox News senior correspondent Eric Shawn reports after a Chinese researcher is sentenced to prison time for pleading guilty to smuggling Escherichia coli (E. coli) into the U.S.

A Customs and Border Protection agriculture detector helped discover nearly 100 pounds of prohibited meat, plants and wildlife products inside luggage arriving from Thailand after alerting officers to the suitcase, authorities said.

CBP said K9 Maisy alerted officers to the bag, which contained 50 pounds of meat, including raw meat, 33 pounds of mangoes, garlic, bamboo, banana plants and approximately 16 pounds of Bengal monitor lizard. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service took custody of the monitor lizard.
"If you discovered all this in a suitcase, wouldn't you be this happy?" CBP wrote alongside a photo of Maisy posing behind the unusual haul.
ONE CANNABIS MISTAKE AT AIRPORT COULD BRING 10 YEARS IN PRISON AND $15,000 FINE

CBP agriculture detector dog Maisy poses behind prohibited meat, plants and wildlife products seized from luggage arriving from Thailand during an inspection by U.S. Customs and Border Protection. (U.S. Customs and Border Protection via Facebook)

CBP agriculture specialists routinely inspect international luggage for prohibited meat, plants and wildlife products that can introduce pests, animal diseases or invasive species into the United States.

In a separate case, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife said officers working with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration inspected a vehicle at the San Ysidro Port of Entry and found approximately 436 fish, including rockfish, lingcod, sheephead and yellowtail.

A California Department of Fish and Wildlife officer examines fish seized during an inspection at the San Ysidro Port of Entry as part of an investigation into the alleged illegal importation of fish from Mexico. (California Department of Fish and Wildlife via Facebook)

MEXICAN NATIONAL SENTENCED IN BORDER CHILD SMUGGLING CASE INVOLVING THC-LACED CANDY

Fish fillets seized by California Department of Fish and Wildlife officers during an inspection at the San Ysidro Port of Entry are displayed inside a cooler as part of an investigation into the alleged illegal importation of fish from Mexico. The agency said the catch was seized as evidence and charges are being pursued in connection with the alleged unlawful take of fish in Mexico, fishing without valid licenses and illegally importing the fish into the United States.

title: Watch: Missouri suspect dives headfirst off bridge in wild bid to evade deputies
summary: Video captures a Missouri man sprinting across a bridge and diving headfirst into Table Rock Lake after leading Stone County deputies on a chase.
story: A Missouri suspect's desperate attempt to escape authorities by diving headfirst off a bridge into the water was captured on dramatic police video before deputies took him into custody. (Stone County Sheriff's Office)
A 26-year-old Missouri man's dramatic attempt to outrun police by diving headfirst off a bridge was caught on video.

Video released by the Stone County Sheriff's Office shows Gavin Thor Lundgren, of Kimberling City, sprinting across a two-lane bridge before launching himself headfirst into the waters of Table Rock Lake after leading deputies on a chase during the early morning hours of July 18.
"This was definitely a first and luckily he survived the fall," the sheriff's office said in a statement. "He resisted arrest and deputies suffered minor injuries taking him into custody."
VIDEO SHOWS ALLEGED CAR THIEF DANGLE UNDER BRIDGE AFTER WILD CHASE, SPARKING TENSE STANDOFF WITH POLICE

Gavin Thor Lundgren is seen diving headfirst off a bridge into Table Rock Lake after allegedly leading Missouri deputies on a pursuit, according to the Stone County Sheriff's Office. (Stone County Sheriff's Office)
Lundgren was arrested and charged with three counts of third-degree assault on a special victim, resisting arrest for a felony, resisting arrest by fleeing and careless driving.
According to a probable cause statement, deputies attempted to stop Lundgren around 1:50 a.m. after spotting his 2004 Chevrolet Malibu traveling nearly 75 mph in a 45-mph zone, according to KOLR.
Instead of pulling over, authorities said Lundgren led deputies on a pursuit before abandoning his still-moving car and diving off the bridge into Table Rock Lake.
FLEEING WISCONSIN DRIVER GETS AIRBORNE AND JUMPS CAR OVER ANOTHER CAR DURING HIGH-SPEED CHASE
Gavin Thor Lundgren was arrested after authorities said he led deputies on a pursuit before diving off a bridge into Table Rock Lake. (Stone County Sheriff's Office)
Three deputies were injured while taking Lundgren into custody, authorities said.
Investigators said Lundgren headbutted two deputies during the struggle.

Gavin Thor Lundgren is seen running across a bridge moments before diving into Table Rock Lake during an alleged attempt to evade Missouri deputies. (Stone County Sheriff's Office)
Officials said deputies suffered injuries including facial bruising, cuts to their hands, elbows and forearms, and abrasions.
Lundgren is being held in the Stone County Jail without bond.

title: Bear caught on camera perched atop New Mexico utility pole before reportedly suffering fatal electrocution
summary: Viral video shows a bear perched atop a utility pole along a rural New Mexico highway, panting and struggling to keep its balance on the precarious perch.
story: The unusual encounter caught on video Monday, July 20, 2026, drew attention online before the bear died after being electrocuted, state wildlife officials said.
A bear that climbed to the top of a utility pole in rural New Mexico became the subject of a viral video this week before reportedly later dying after the unusual encounter.

The video, recorded Monday near Gladstone, New Mexico, roughly 170 miles east of Santa Fe, shows the bear precariously perched on the crossarm of the utility pole while panting and trying to maintain its balance high above the ground.
The U.S. Department of the Interior shared the video Wednesday, joking, "We appreciate the enthusiasm for American Energy Dominance, but this isn't what we meant."
WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA
A bear perches atop a utility pole near Gladstone, N.M., after climbing the pole in a bizarre encounter captured on video. (Shannon Mullens via Storyful)
The Department of the Interior and the New Mexico Department of Wildlife did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.
The footage, verified by Storyful, also includes audio from a 911 caller reporting the unusual sight.
"I'm calling to report a bear on top of a light pole," the caller tells a dispatcher.
WOMAN STALKED BY CHARGING BEAR ON MORNING DOG WALK CAPTURES TERRIFYING ENCOUNTER ON CAMERA
A bear balances atop a utility pole near Gladstone, N.M., in video captured by a passing motorist before the unusual encounter drew widespread attention online. (Shannon Mullens via Storyful)
The dispatcher responded that state officials had already been notified but said tranquilizing the animal while it remained atop the pole could have caused it to fall.

Shannon Mullens, who recorded the video, told Storyful she was traveling from Red River, New Mexico, to Oklahoma on Highway 56 when she and her family spotted what they initially believed was a dead bear.
"We really didn't believe what we saw at first, so we turned around to get another look," Mullens said.
HIDDEN DANGER AT POPULAR US NATIONAL PARK FORCES TRAIL CLOSURES AS BEAR SIGHTINGS CLIMB
The bear hangs from the crossarm of a utility pole in rural New Mexico during the unusual incident that later drew widespread attention online. (Shannon Mullens via Storyful)
"At first, we thought that the bear was dead, until we got closer to it, and then we realized that he was still alive."
The bear was electrocuted and died before wildlife officials could safely rescue it, the New York Post reported.

Wildlife experts say bears can climb utility poles after becoming startled by people, traffic or dogs, treating them much like trees while trying to escape danger.
A similar incident ended differently in Arizona in 2021, when wildlife officials safely rescued a bear that had climbed a utility pole.

title: Teachers who once dated and share child arrested after classroom argument spiraled into violence: police
summary: Both teachers at The SEED School of Miami face domestic violence battery charges after an alleged assault and pepper spray attack on school property.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A personal dispute between two teachers who were formerly a couple erupted inside a Miami charter boarding school, ending with both under arrest after investigators say a classroom meeting turned violent.

According to a Miami-Dade Schools Police arrest affidavit obtained by Fox News Digital, Terrod Tiyan Torrence, 36, and Odiria Biggins were previously involved in a romantic relationship and share a child together.
A few days before the confrontation, Biggins told investigators Torrence left a handwritten note on her desk asking if they could talk.
She agreed to meet him July 17 inside Classroom 119 at The SEED School of Miami, the affidavit said.
SJSU VOLLEYBALL COACH'S ALLEGED ASSAULT VICTIM SPEAKS OUT FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE ALLEGATIONS SURFACED

Terrod Torrence was charged with domestic violence after investigators say a confrontation with a fellow teacher at The SEED School of Miami turned physical. (Miami-Dade County Corrections and Rehabilitation)
What began as a conversation quickly turned physical, according to investigators.
Biggins told police Torrence repeatedly punched her in the left side of the head before slamming her head into a wall, causing her to lose consciousness and collapse to the floor.
MARCELLUS WILEY'S WIFE CLAIMS EX-NFL STAR THREATENED TO KILL HER BEFORE FOURTH OF JULY DOMESTIC BATTERY ARREST
But the confrontation didn't end there, investigators said.

After regaining consciousness, Biggins allegedly walked to her vehicle, grabbed a canister of pepper spray and later tracked Torrence down elsewhere on campus before spraying him, according to Miami ABC affiliate WSVN.
Surveillance video captured Biggins entering a classroom where Torrence was, the outlet reported.
BRING THE BEAR SPRAY TO THE WEDDING — YOU NEVER KNOW WHEN YOU NEED TO USE IT ON A FAMILY MEMBER
A courtyard at The SEED School of Miami, where investigators say an argument between two teachers escalated into violence. (The SEED School of Miami Facebook)
Moments later, both emerged with Torrence appearing to struggle walking and suffering visible eye irritation before school staff rushed to help him. He was later taken to a hospital for treatment.

Biggins was arrested Monday and charged with discharging a weapon on school property for allegedly using pepper spray on campus, along with misdemeanor domestic violence battery, according to WSVN. A judge found probable cause and set her bond at $2,000.
Torrence was arrested Tuesday by Miami-Dade Schools Police and charged with misdemeanor domestic violence battery.
The Miami-Dade Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center (Google Maps)

Court records show he was booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center before appearing before Judge Alicia Garcia Priovolos, who imposed a $2,000 standard bond and a pretrial no-contact order barring him from contacting Biggins. His arraignment is scheduled for Sept. 23.

It remains unclear what sparked the argument or whether any students witnessed the confrontation.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Miami-Dade Schools Police Department and The SEED School of Miami for additional information, including whether either teacher remains employed.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Woman who stole $1.7M meant for hurricane victims gets prison time as DHS cracks down on FEMA fraud
summary: Jasmine Williams submitted fraudulent documents for nearly 200 people after Hurricane Ida, demanding half of each FEMA payout in a $1.7 million scheme.
story: The Trump administration boosts efforts in its 'war on fraud,' including independent journalist Nick Shirley's Senate testimony exposing rampant tax dollar misuse. Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald reveals over $1 billion recovered from trade fraud.

FIRST ON FOX: A Pennsylvania woman who defrauded the federal government out of $1.7 million in Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) funds in the wake of Hurricane Ida was sentenced to five years in prison, the Justice Department said Wednesday as the Trump administration continues its effort to crack down on fraud.
Jasmine Williams, 34, of Plymouth Meeting, pleaded guilty last year to 32 charges ranging from fraud related to a major disaster declaration to wire fraud and mail fraud.

"Under the leadership of President [Donald] Trump and Secretary [Markwayne] Mullin, FEMA is rooting out fraud in disaster aid," Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Assistant Secretary Lauren Bis exclusively told Fox News Digital.

"We are protecting taxpayer dollars and making sure disaster assistance goes to those who truly need it," Bis continued. "Anyone who tries to steal from survivors will be caught and held accountable."
MINNESOTA OF THE CARIBBEAN? TRUMP ADMIN FREEZES VACATION HOT SPOT’S FUNDS OVER ALLEGED HURRICANE-AID ABUSES

A Blue FEMA tarp covers the roof of a home more than a week after Hurricane Irma made landfall. A Pennsylvania woman was sentenced to five years in prison for defrauding FEMA in the aftermath of the storm. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
President Joe Biden issued a disaster declaration in September 2021 after the remnants of Hurricane Ida struck much of the eastern portion of the state.

Officials said Williams solicited participants in her scheme — renters, homeowners or the homeless — and submitted fraudulent documents to FEMA on behalf of almost 200 others, including fraudulent leases, letters from landlords, utility bills, earning statements and home repair estimates.
She recruited the participants over social media, advertising that she could assist them in applying for FEMA benefits, prosecutors said.
TRUMP SAYS ANTI-FRAUD EFFORTS ARE UNCOVERING BILLIONS IN WASTE, CLAIMS SAVINGS COULD BALANCE BUDGET
President Joe Biden speaks during a virtual Hurricane Ida briefing at the White House in Washington, D.C., Aug. 30, 2021. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)
As part of the fraud, she requested half of the payout for herself, amassing hundreds of thousands of dollars.
When one person involved in the scheme didn’t pay her, Williams posted that person's personal information on social media, officials said.
She also posted a video criticizing the person for not paying the 50% Williams charged.
Williams additionally used social media to solicit images of damaged homes to submit in support of her fraudulent applications, federal prosecutors said.

In fiscal year 2025, FEMA identified more than 1,700 fraud cases.

title: Travelers unite in powerful moment of silence as fallen US service member returns home
summary: Video captured hundreds of travelers at Raleigh-Durham International Airport standing in silence during a dignified transfer. The clip gained attention online.
story: A large group of travelers at Raleigh-Durham International Airport stood in silence, many with their hands over their hearts, during the dignified transfer of a fallen American service member. (Credit: The White House)
A powerful display of respect unfolded inside a busy North Carolina airport as strangers united to honor a fallen American service member's final journey home.

Video shared by the White House and many others on social media shows a large group of travelers gathered along the terminal windows at Raleigh-Durham International Airport, many with their hands over their hearts, during the dignified transfer of a fallen service member on the tarmac below.

"BEAUTIFUL MOMENT: Hundreds of Americans at Raleigh-Durham International Airport stood in silence to honor a fallen service member as they returned home," the White House wrote Wednesday in a post on Instagram. "A grateful nation remembers. God bless our troops."
The moving tribute quickly drew an outpouring of emotional reactions online, with many commenters praising the travelers who paused their own journeys to pay their respects.
GOLD STAR WIDOW SAYS 'BLESSINGS ARE INFINITE' AFTER STRANGERS FLOOD HUSBAND'S ARLINGTON GRAVE
"God bless and comfort these families. I am so thankful for their service. The dark will not outshine the light!" one person wrote.
"There is hope for the USA. God bless our fallen heroes," another commenter added.
AS AN ARMY WIDOW, I WILL NEVER FORGET HOW ORDINARY AMERICANS HONORED MY HUSBAND
Others said the tribute left them emotional.
"This brought me to tears," one person wrote.

The United Service Organizations (USO) confirmed to Fox News Digital that its Raleigh-Durham Airport Center Honors Support Team assisted with a dignified transfer at the airport on July 21 but declined to identify the fallen service member.
PENTAGON IDENTIFIES ARMY SOLDIER KILLED IN ACTION DURING IRAQ OPERATION

Travelers at Raleigh-Durham International Airport stand in silence, many with their hands over their hearts, as a dignified transfer for a fallen U.S. service member takes place on the tarmac outside. (The White House via Instagram)
"Out of respect for the service member, the family and military notification procedures, we are unable to provide additional information regarding the individual or the transfer," the USO said.
The organization said its staff and volunteers are prepared to support military families during some of their most difficult moments.

"When a service member makes their final journey home, our staff and volunteers are prepared to provide compassionate support to families and work alongside our military partners to help ensure a dignified transfer and the respectful honoring of our nation’s fallen," the USO said.
The organization added that it works to ease logistical burdens and provide families with a welcoming space and essential services so they can focus on honoring their loved one.
The airport tribute came as the nation mourned four U.S. service members recently killed during the war with Iran.

Earlier Wednesday, the Department of War's Rapid Response account announced that four American service members who "made the ultimate sacrifice for our nation" had been welcomed home during dignified transfer ceremonies.
"Today, we welcomed home four brave Americans who made the ultimate sacrifice for our nation," the account wrote on X. "Their courage will never be forgotten."

North Carolina Senate candidate Michael Whatley honored Swinton in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

"May God Bless Sgt. Michael Swinton and his family," Whatley said. "North Carolina and the country owe an immeasurable debt to those who have given their lives to protect and preserve the liberties which make America the greatest nation on Earth."

An African migrant upset over being unable to cancel his monthly $65 parking garage contract allegedly shot and killed three property managers at his Minnesota apartment building over the dispute, authorities said.

Tsegaab Ademassu Binessu, 30, was charged with three counts of second-degree murder with intent following the alleged slayings Monday of Nansi G. Fuentes Zambrano, 25, Dena M. Silcox, 56, and 43-year-old Adam J. Wilwerding at the St. Paul complex, court documents state.

The rampage began after Binessu, from Ethiopia, called the apartment building staffers to cancel his $65 monthly parking contract because he had sold his car. He was told he could not do so after recently renewing the agreement.
Despite being told the contract could not be canceled, Binessu said he would be going to the management office in person, prosecutors said.

Once there, he allegedly opened fire, killing all three victims. Police later found 21, 9 mm shell casings in the leasing office.

Shortly after the shooting, a man called the police stating that he had been Binessu's roommate since 2018. He said Binessu, who had aspirations of joining the U.S. Navy, called him and confessed to the triple murder, adding that he was walking to the police station.
Binessu worked as a trucker but quit two months ago, the roommate told authorities, and had planned on enlisting in the military. He sold his car the same day as the shooting, police said.

Surveillance footage reviewed by investigators captured Binessu talking with Silcox and Wilwerding.
At some point, Binessu allegedly pulled up his shirt, grabbed his gun from his waistband, pointed the weapon at Wilwerding, who put his hands in front of his body, and shot him three times.
Binessu then fired three more times as Wilwerding fell to the floor, court documents said.
Silcox screamed and covered her ears when Binessu allegedly shot Wilwerding, saying, "No, no — no, no, no."
Binessu is then accused of shooting Silcox five times in rapid succession, according to court documents. As she wheeled her chair away from the desk, Binessu allegedly shot her a sixth time.

Binessu stalked around the office and said, "Motherf------ b----," court documents said. He then moved toward a hallway out of the camera's view, where a woman's screams could be heard followed by four more gunshots.

Prosecutors said Binessu was arrested while driving Fuentes Zambrano's car, which contained what appeared to be newly purchased camping gear, according to the charges. Inside the vehicle, authorities found his U.S. passport, Social Security card, an empty handgun magazine and his gun permit.

title: US soldier killed in Jordan attack remembered as living 'life of courage and selflessness'
summary: Tributes are coming in for Sgt. Angel Rampersad, who was killed in action during an "enemy attack" at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.
story: The U.S. has launched strikes on Iranian targets following attacks that killed three American service members in Jordan and Iraq.
The American soldier who was killed in Jordan during an Iranian attack is being remembered as living a "life of courage and selflessness."

The Department of War announced that Sgt. Angel Rampersad, 28, of Ozone Park, New York, is one of the three soldiers "killed in action on July 17, 2026, during an enemy attack at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base" in Jordan. U.S. Central Command said over the weekend that the service members died as CENTCOM and partner forces "defended against Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks."

"Sgt. Rampersad lived a life of courage and selflessness. New York, and our nation, are safer because of brave Americans like her who answer the call to serve," New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said in a statement. "May we honor her memory, remember her sacrifice and keep all who loved her in our prayers."
"My heart is with her family, loved ones and the soldiers who stood beside her as they grieve this unimaginable loss," Hochul added.
ARMY IDENTIFIES VICTIMS KILLED IN JORDAN AIR BASE ATTACK

The Department of War said "Sgt. Angel Rampersad, 28, of Ozone Park, New York, is believed to have been killed in action on July 17, 2026, during an enemy attack at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Jordan." (10th Army Air and Missile Defense Command)

"Sgt. Rampersad's courage and sacrifice will be remembered not just in Queens, but across all five boroughs," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. "My deepest condolences are with her family, loved ones, and all those grieving this profound loss. For so many New Yorkers, wars overseas are never distant -- they are felt here at home. The sacrifices made by service members and their families are a constant reminder of this. We are forever grateful for their service and will work every day to honor it."

The Department of War said the incident leading to Rampersad’s death is under investigation and that she was previously identified as missing. The other two soldiers believed to have been killed in the attack were identified as 1st Lt. Tyler James Feehan, 25, of Ewa Beach, Hawaii, and Pvt. Isabella Gonzales, 19, of Carrollton, Texas. They were in Jordan supporting Operation Inherent Resolve, the international campaign against ISIS in Iraq and Syria.

"Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over!" Trump wrote Monday on Truth Social. "This directive has been passed on to Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Daniel Caine, and every Leader in the Military."
PENTAGON IDENTIFIES ARMY SOLDIER KILLED IN ACTION DURING IRAQ OPERATION
Lt. Tyler James Feehan, 25, of Ewa Beach, Hawaii, and Pvt. Isabella Gonzales, 19, of Carrollton, Texas, were also "killed in action" in Jordan, according to the U.S. Army. (U.S. Army)

Rampersad was assigned to 1st Battalion, 57th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 52d Air Defense Artillery Brigade, 10th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, Ansbach, Germany, and served as a 25U Signal Operations Support Specialist, according to the Department of War.

"Today, we mourn the loss of Sgt. Angel Rampersad," Brig. Gen. Glenn Henke, commanding general of the 10th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, said in a statement. "We extend our deepest, most heartfelt condolences to her family and all those who are navigating this unimaginable loss. title: Trump administration has lost or abandoned hundreds of lawsuits against anti-ICE protesters, migrants: report
summary: A report said the Trump administration lost or abandoned hundreds of cases charging anti-ICE protesters and migrants with assaulting agents.
story: Former Acting DHS Secretary Chad Wolf discusses the White House's new guidance allowing I.C.E. agents to resume traffic stops if at least one agent is wearing a body camera following recent fatal shootings on 'America Reports.'
The Trump administration has lost or abandoned hundreds of cases in which it accused anti-ICE protesters and migrants of assaulting federal immigration agents, a report said.

An analysis from The New York Times showed that of the 558 people charged, 191 cases were dismissed, and 22 people were acquitted. Only four were convicted after trial, while 246 pleaded guilty and another 95 cases are pending.

The newspaper reported the Justice Department typically has a record of more than 90% of defendants pleading guilty or being convicted at trial. The Trump administration’s strategy in court has been leaning on 18 U.S.C. 111, a statute that makes it a federal crime to assault or forcibly impede a government officer and carries punishments ranging from a fine to 20 years in prison, it added.

Department of Homeland Security Assistant Secretary Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital on Wednesday that "It should come as no surprise that there’s an increase in criminal referrals under 18 U.S.C. 111 as there’s been a massive increase in violence and threats against federal law enforcement."

"ICE officers are facing a more than 1,300% increase in assaults, a 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them," she added. "Assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime and felony. Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law."
NEW YORK TIMES TORCHED FOR 'FALSE' REPORTING ON ICE INVESTIGATIONS, OUTLET FIRES BACK

Federal agents are seen walking in uniform. A report from The New York Times said the Trump administration has lost or abandoned hundreds of cases in which it accused anti-ICE protesters and migrants of assaulting federal immigration agents. (John Moore/Getty Images)

"Federal prosecutors are correct to prioritize these prosecutions and hold individuals accountable to the fullest extent of the law," Justice Department spokesman Wyn Hornbuckle told the New York Times, describing how prosecutors, at times, reduced or dropped charges based on "mitigating factors identified in a case."
The New York Times cited another Justice Department official as saying that prosecutors in some of the cases dropped charges when the defendants were deported from the United States.
The newspaper said it based its analysis on court filings, hearing transcripts, videos of encounters and interviews with witnesses and federal officials.
ICE RESUMES NATIONWIDE TRAFFIC STOPS UNDER NEW POLICY REQUIRING BODY CAMERAS

A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent during a multi-agency targeted enforcement operation in Chicago, Illinois on Sunday, Jan. 26, 2025. (Christopher Dilts/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

It reported that in dozens of the cases that were lost or abandoned, court records and video showed that federal agents initiated physical struggles, such as shoving, tackling and pepper spraying defendants. Other defendants were able to successfully argue that the assaults they were accused of committing against the federal agents were acts of self-defense, the newspaper added.
Two of the judges overseeing the cases discovered agents purposely destroyed evidence, including demanding that a defendant delete images from their cellphone, according to The New York Times.

Officers also charged more than two dozen people who allegedly filmed or followed agents, sometimes honking car horns or shouting phrases like, "La migra is coming!," despite no allegations of physical contact with agents, the newspaper reported.

In one case, a judge dismissed assault charges against an immigrant after ruling that the agent involved was cut by glass from a car window that the agent had smashed, and in 65 instances, prosecutors abandoned or dropped charges before deadlines to present evidence to a grand jury or judge, the New York Times also said.
Anti-I.C.E. protesters face off with federal agents outside the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement building on Oct. 18, 2025, in Portland, Oregon. (Mathieu Lewis-Rolland/Getty)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The report did note one occasion when federal immigration officers were seriously hurt by protesters and migrants, including the dragging of an officer who had his arm inside a car window.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: ‘Hero' mom dies after using last strength to save 4-year-old son from Florida river
summary: Nicole Grayson, 43, jumped into the St. Johns River at Ed Stone Park to save her 4-year-old son, using all her strength to keep him above water.
story: ICE officer Gregory Simmonds describes the heroic moment he rescued a 6-year-old from drowning in a Florida pool on May 16, as captured by surveillance video. Simmonds jumped in fully clothed, pulled the unconscious child out and performed CPR to save the child's life. He also addresses current criticisms facing the agency.

A Florida "hero" mom died after using all her strength to keep her 4-year-old son above water when he fell into the St. Johns River, allowing rescuers to pull the boy to safety, authorities and her family said.
Nicole Grayson, 43, jumped into the river after her young son fell into the water at Ed Stone Park, west of DeLand, around 4 p.m. Saturday, according to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office.

Investigators said the child had been playing with an unidentified object near a wooden fence along the river’s edge when he dropped it over the barrier. The boy fell into the river while attempting to retrieve it.
OFF-DUTY ICE OFFICER RELIES ON 'SIXTH SENSE' TO SAVE DROWNING CHILD BEFORE DELIVERING MESSAGE TO CRITICS
Grayson immediately went in after him.
Nicole Grayson drowned after rescuing her 4-year-old son from the St. Johns River in Central Florida. (GoFundMe)

"My guess is he was trying to get it. He slipped in the water, deep, he slipped away in the water," Grayson’s oldest son, Dafino Devega, told FOX 35. "And then my mom, I guess she panicked, and she went in the water and tried to save him."
CROCODILE ATTACK HORROR UNFOLDS AS COUPLE TRIES TO SAVE VICTIM: ‘WE FELT SO HELPLESS’
As Grayson struggled to keep her son above the surface, a witness at the park flagged down a passing boater, who threw two life preservers toward the mother and child, the sheriff’s office said.
Grayson eventually became submerged while continuing to hold her son above the water.
A frantic 911 caller told dispatchers that rescuers had managed to reach the child but were still struggling to recover his mother.
FIREFIGHTERS, POLICE PULL YOUNG WOMAN FROM SEWAGE-FILLED RAVINE AFTER DAYS TRAPPED IN 104-DEGREE HEAT
"Hey 911, can you come to Ed Stone Park?" the caller said in audio obtained by FOX 35. "We have a mother that’s drowned, and we got the baby, but we can’t get the mama."

A memorial of daisies is placed near a fence where Volusia sheriff's deputies said a 4-year-old fell over into the St. Johns River on July 18. The child's mother drowned after she jumped in to save her son, according to deputies. (Patricio G. Balona / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

The boater maneuvered close enough to pull the 4-year-old aboard. The boy was unharmed, according to authorities.
Witness Jon Reaka said Grayson appeared to expend all her energy ensuring her son survived.
"She spent all her energy trying to get her kid up over the edge," Reaka told FOX 35.
Reaka jumped over a railing and onto the boat, where he helped pull Grayson from the river. She was unresponsive when she was brought aboard.

"I jumped over the rail, jumped onto the boat and pulled the lady up onto the boat and, you know, we started CPR — I started CPR and mouth-to-mouth immediately," Reaka said.
Emergency medical personnel took over lifesaving measures after arriving at the park. Grayson was rushed to a hospital, where efforts to revive her continued for several hours.
She died in the intensive care unit around 10 p.m. Saturday, the sheriff’s office said.

"I tried everything I could do to save her," Reaka told FOX 35. "You know, I feel horrible. I mean, it’s so sad what happened."
Grayson was a mother of six whose final act reflected the fiercely protective way she had lived, her family said.
"That’s the type of mom that she was; she was a hero," Devega said.
"My mom, she was a strong woman," he added. "She would do anything to keep her kids safe."

Volusia County Sheriff Mike Chitwood praised the witnesses and the boater who rushed to help Grayson and her son.

"Sheriff Chitwood and the entire Volusia Sheriff's Office send sincere thanks all who jumped in to help with the rescue, and deepest condolences to Ms. Grayson's family and friends for their loss of a mother who gave her life to save her son," the department said in a statement.

Chitwood said Grayson would be remembered as a hero, "not just because of her final heroic act, but because she was a mom who would do anything for her kids."

title: Woman's remains identified by DNA in Virginia, exposing second alleged murder linked to same 4 suspects
summary: DNA analysis identified Helen Marie Pullen Banks months after her remains were found, linking her death to four suspects in a second Virginia murder.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

The four suspects accused of killing a Virginia teenager are now facing charges in a second homicide after investigators identified a woman whose remains remained a mystery for more than three months, revealing what authorities say were two connected, premeditated killings.

Helen Marie Pullen Banks, 56, of Culpeper, was identified through "extensive and complex DNA analysis" completed July 7, after her remains were discovered March 27 on private property in Caroline County, according to the sheriff's office.

Authorities announced this month that Rashad Antonio Mayfield, 21, Devonti Gregory Pettaway, 19, Jaden Lamont Phillips, 20, and Kennady Jade Lambert, 18, have each been charged with first-degree murder, conspiracy to commit murder and use of a firearm in the commission of murder in Banks' death.
WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT

Authorities say Kennady Jade Lambert, Devonti Gregory Pettaway, Jaden Lamont Phillips and Rashad Antonio Mayfield are charged in the murders of Helen Marie Pullen Banks and Jayden McComber. (Google Maps/Caroline County Sheriff's Office, VA)
All four suspects were already being held without bond after being charged with murder in the death of 18-year-old Jayden McComber.
Investigators say they suspected early in the case that the two homicide investigations were linked.

McComber disappeared the same day Banks' remains were discovered. His vehicle was recovered the following day in Virginia Beach with assistance from the Virginia Beach Police Department, according to the sheriff's office.
TEENS SUSPECTED OF MURDERING CONGRESSIONAL INTERN LINKED BY DNA ON SHELL CASINGS, PROSECUTORS SAY
Jayden McComber was 18 years old when he was killed in March 2026, according to investigators. (Virginia State Police)
Authorities said the vehicle was thoroughly processed and produced "valuable investigative leads" that helped investigators locate McComber's remains and identify the suspects.
McComber's body was found March 31 in a pond near the Caroline County line.

During an April 2 search of a Henrico County residence believed to be associated with Mayfield, investigators recovered personal belongings thought to have been in McComber's possession when he disappeared, authorities said.

Mayfield was arrested on charges during a traffic stop conducted while investigators were searching the residence. Authorities said a handgun was seized from his possession, though they have not disclosed whether the firearm has been linked to either homicide.

Pettaway, Phillips and Lambert were arrested during a simultaneous operation at an apartment on Kenway Avenue in Henrico. Caroline County investigators were assisted in the arrests by the U.S. Marshals Service Capital Area Regional Fugitive Task Force.

Following the arrests, Sheriff Scott Moser described the case as a "complex and difficult investigation" and praised the "relentless work" that led authorities to the four suspects.
The sheriff's office said ballistic testing performed with assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives later produced forensic evidence linking the two murders.

Investigators say both Banks and McComber knew at least one of the suspects before they were killed. However, authorities said they have uncovered no evidence that either victim had a conflict or dispute with the suspects over what investigators described as "premeditated and deliberate acts."
Authorities have not disclosed a possible motive or said whether Banks and McComber knew one another.
When Banks' remains were first discovered, the property owner who found them was "understandably shaken" and did not approach the body before calling 911, according to the sheriff's office.

"This is a deeply disturbing case," Moser said at the time. "The scene our deputies and investigators encountered was difficult, but they remained focused and professional from the moment they arrived."
Helen Marie Pullen Banks' identity remained unknown for more than three months before investigators identified her through DNA analysis. (Found and Sons Funeral Chapels & Cremation Service)

The sheriff's office later alleged that those responsible had taken "sick and deliberate" measures to conceal Banks' identity, calling it one of the more disturbing cases investigators had encountered. Authorities have not publicly detailed those alleged measures.
Banks' identity was formally confirmed July 7, and investigators met with her family that evening to notify them.

"This case reflects the relentless commitment of our investigators to pursue the truth," Moser said after announcing the identification. "While no announcement can ease the pain of this loss, we hope today's identification of Helen Marie Pullen Banks provides at least some measure of answers for her loved ones."

The investigation has also involved the Caroline County Commonwealth's Attorney's Office, FBI and ATF. Authorities said they are not searching for any additional suspects, though the case remains active.
The sheriff's office said Banks' family was notified of her identification on July 7 after DNA testing confirmed her identity.

Banks was born in Charlottesville and lived in Rixeyville, according to her obituary. She is survived by five children, her mother, two siblings, 10 grandchildren, one great-grandchild and a large extended family.
Helen Marie Pullen Banks, 56, was identified through DNA testing after her remains were discovered in Caroline County. (GoFundMe)

"Helen was so much more than the circumstances surrounding her passing," her family wrote in a GoFundMe established to help cover memorial expenses. "She was a daughter, a sister, a mother, a grandmother, and a great-grandmother."
McComber's family also remembered the 18-year-old in a GoFundMe created after his death, describing the week-long search for him as "a nightmare no family should ever have to live through."

"Jayden was so deeply loved," his family wrote. "He had the biggest heart and made sure the people around him knew it. He never missed a chance to say 'I love you,' and those words mean everything to us now."
The investigation remains active, though authorities say they are not seeking additional suspects.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Caroline County Sheriff's Office, the Caroline County Commonwealth's Attorney's Office, the Virginia Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, the FBI, ATF, the Virginia Beach Police Department and court officials for additional information.

title: Alleged 'mime' stalker stripped to underwear, covered himself in cooking oil: officials
summary: Massachusetts man Hernan Villagran Lux allegedly stripped to his underwear and slathered cooking oil on his body near female park workers before collapsing in court.
story: Hernan Villagran Lux, 29, was arrested by Massachusetts State Police on Sunday evening and appeared to faint on the stand in court this week. (Boston 25)
Not all mimes stay silent. One is now accused of terrorizing women.

A Massachusetts man known for roaming in a black-and-white mime costume is accused of frightening women for months at a popular state park, where prosecutors say he allegedly stripped to his underwear, slathered himself in cooking oil and worked out near female employees before later collapsing in court as the allegations were read aloud.

Hernan Villagran Lux, 29, of Framingham, is facing criminal harassment charges after three female state Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) employees had up to over 50 encounters over the past two months at a Natick state park near Boston.

Prosecutors said all three women knew Lux by name and appearance, and one reported more than 50 encounters that authorities said escalated over time, eventually leaving employees afraid to work around him.
FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES
Appearing in court earlier this week, alleged "mime" stalker Hernan Villagran Lux, 29, fainted on the stand as his charges were read. (Boston 25 News)

The allegations have also sparked warnings on social media, where people across several Massachusetts communities said they recognized the suspect and claimed he had approached or followed women on a nearby rail trail.

Authorities arrested Lux Sunday night on the Cochituate Rail Trail, after multiple women and park workers alleged he repeatedly approached them, stared at them and refused to leave despite repeated requests, according to Boston 25 News.

"The women report an extensive number of contacts with the defendant involving him staring at them, smiling in what they describe as 'a really unnerving and frankly terrifying manner,'" Framingham District Court Supervisor Andrew Mange said during Monday's court hearing.
MAN ACCUSED OF REPEATEDLY TRESPASSING AT CIA HEADQUARTERS IN VIRGINIA
A sign marks the entrance to Cochituate State Park in Natick, Mass., where a man is accused of repeatedly harassing female park employees over several months. (Boston 25 News)

Mange said the encounters became increasingly bold. In one incident, prosecutors allege Lux "stripped down to his underwear, slathered cooking oil all over his body and began working out right by their staff area."
The women also reported that Lux repeatedly refused to leave the park after being asked to do so, according to the station.
Prosecutors also alleged Lux complimented one employee's appearance, commented on her lips and refused to leave as she and coworkers abandoned their work area because they felt unsafe.
Boston 25 reported that numerous people posted on social media saying they had spotted a man matching Lux's distinctive mime-like appearance throughout Framingham, Natick and Wayland.
Several women also claimed a man fitting the same description approached and followed them on the Cochituate Rail Trail.

Hernan Villagran Lux appears in Framingham District Court in Framingham, Mass., on criminal harassment charges stemming from allegations involving female employees at a state park outside Boston. (Boston 25 News)
"I spotted him, he looked kind of odd but I thought he was just dressed in a costume," neighbor Nancy Dlott told Boston 25. "It's kind of upsetting, especially if you're walking alone," she added.
"I just don't understand what goes through someone's head to do that," Christopher Labella told the station. "I hope this guy gets the help that he needs."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
As prosecutors continued reading the allegations in court Monday, Lux fainted and was treated before proceedings resumed, according to Boston 25.
When court resumed later in the afternoon, the judge ordered Lux to undergo a mental health evaluation at Bridgewater State Hospital.

title: California toddler bitten by rattlesnake hiding beneath Amazon package amid active snake season
summary: A 3-year-old girl was bitten by a rattlesnake hiding beneath an Amazon package outside her California home and spent two days receiving antivenom.
story: Jesse Watters reports on a significant increase in snake bites across the United States this summer, noting that California has already exceeded its yearly quota for fatal bites. Watters details the severe injuries sustained by Chris, who required 36 vials of antivenom after a Western rattlesnake bite, and a 2-year-old girl in Colorado who was airlifted to the hospital following a rattlesnake attack.

A Southern California family is urging people to stay alert after their 3-year-old daughter was bitten by a rattlesnake hiding beneath an Amazon package outside their home, the latest in a string of snakebite incidents during an unusually active season across the state.
The frightening encounter comes weeks after a hiker was airlifted from a remote Ventura County trail following a rattlesnake bite.

Earlier this year, Ventura County firefighters told Fox News Digital they had responded to seven rattlesnake bites in roughly a month, and officials attributed the increase to warmer weather that has driven snakes out earlier than usual.

Manuel Barajas said his daughter, Addy, ran outside after her mother told her an Amazon package had been delivered and tossed over the family's front gate. As the 3-year-old reached for the padded envelope, a Southern Pacific rattlesnake concealed beneath it bit her on the left hand.
TOURIST DIES AT LUXURY RESORT AFTER COBRA FROM SNAKE SHOW CLIMBS UP PANTS, BITES HIM: POLICE

A Southern Pacific rattlesnake is held by a wrangler in Landers, Calif. A 3-year-old California girl was recently bitten by the species after it hid beneath an Amazon package outside her home. (Gina Ferazzi/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images, File)

Her mother rushed Addy to a nearby grocery store parking lot, where paramedics met the family before transporting her to a hospital. She was later transferred to a pediatric intensive care unit, where she spent two days receiving additional doses of antivenom.

Wildlife experts say an unusually warm spring has fueled increased rattlesnake activity across California this year, contributing to a rise in snakebite incidents and three reported snakebite deaths statewide.

The latest incident follows several other serious encounters this year. In May, a woman hiking in Ventura County was airlifted to a hospital after being bitten by a rattlesnake on a remote trail. A Thousand Oaks woman also died in March after being bitten while hiking at Wildwood Regional Park.
TICK BITE ER VISITS HIT HIGHEST SEASONAL LEVEL IN YEARS AS DOCTORS WARN OF DISEASE SURGE
The snake was underneath a padded Amazon package when it lunged at the 3-year-old child. (Lindsey Nicholson/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images, File)
Health officials say anyone bitten by a rattlesnake should seek emergency medical care immediately, remain as still as possible and avoid attempting home remedies that can worsen the injury.

Barajas told Nexstar's KTLA he hopes sharing his family's experience will encourage others to stay vigilant around their homes and know which hospitals are equipped to treat pediatric snakebite emergencies.
Experts say California has seen increased rattlesnake activity this year. (Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images, File)

"She’s doing great now. She’s, I want to say, about 70% recovered," Barajas said. "She’s still bruised on her left hand where she was bitten. Her spirits are high, her demeanor is great, but she keeps asking why she was bitten by a snake."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A GoFundMe campaign has been launched to help the family cover Addy's medical expenses and lost income while she continues to recover.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Army veteran faces arson charge after attack outside NYC federal building: 'Came armed with bad intentions'
summary: Videos show fire and bright orange flames outside 26 Federal Plaza as Andrew Arrabaca allegedly fired an airsoft rifle at the federal building.
story: Video shows suspect Andrew Arrabaca allegedly pouring gasoline and setting a fire outside Manhattan’s 16 Federal Plaza, home to New York City’s immigrant court and ICE offices.

The U.S. Army veteran accused of setting a fire outside a New York City federal building that houses an immigration court and other government agencies, including the FBI, and firing a pellet gun, will face an arson charge related to the Monday attack, which he had been planning for months, federal prosecutors said.
Andrew Arrabaca, 43, appeared in a Manhattan federal court Tuesday for his alleged actions outside 26 Federal Plaza that injured three people before he was subdued.
He did not enter a plea.
U.S. Magistrate Judge Robyn F. Tarnofsky, noted that the attack could have ended tragically.

"The crime you’re charged with is troubling," said Tarnofsky, who immediately conducted a bail hearing and ordered Arrabaca to be released to a mental health facility. The judge said the alleged attack was "planned over time" and "wasn't something that was done on a Sunday."
FBI ARRESTS PROTESTER WHO THREATENED TO KILL ICE OFFICER'S FAMILY AT NJ DETENTION CENTER PROTEST, BLANCHE SAYS
Authorities apprehended a suspect outside a federal building in New York City on Monday. (FNTV)

Arrabaca, who served as a mechanic on Patriot missile systems in the Army, harbored anti-ICE and anti-government views, James Barnacle, assistant director in charge of the FBI's New York Field Office, said Monday.
"He is an anti-American, anti-government extremist," Barnacle told reporters at the scene.
Voter records show he has registered as a Democrat and was a member of the left-wing Working Families party.
Andrew Arrabaca, 43, is charged with arson for allegedly setting a fire outside 26 Federal Plaza in New York City on Monday.  (Justice Department)

Arrabaca "came armed with bad intentions" and was found with a range of weapons, including a pellet gun, knives, a hammer, and a machete. Authorities said the upstate New York resident arrived at the federal building sometime around 8:30 a.m. and lit a large firework before pouring a liquid that ignited a fire.
Videos and images from the scene showed a fire with a plume of smoke and bright orange flames near a building entrance, as well as law enforcement officers restraining the suspect.
VIDEO SHOWS MOMENT CHICAGO MAN ALLEGEDLY USED SUV AS WEAPON AGAINST ICE AGENT, PROSECUTORS SAY

In addition to allegedly setting the fire, Arrabaca also fired five to seven pellets from an airsoft rifle toward the building, Barnacle said. He was arrested by federal officials a short time later and has been in custody since.

He made several anti-government and anti-ICE statements during the incident and said "he was okay if he hurt or killed people going in and out of the building, whether they were federal employees or civilians," the FBI said.
Upon his arrest, authorities said they found Arrabaca with two axes, a hammer, a machete and three knives.

Prosecutors said he had arrived pulling a four-wheeled utility wagon bearing a sign that read "ICE Off Our Streets," which also contained BB and pellet rifles, fireworks and a consumer firework labeled "Nuclear Warhead." Arrabaca was also wearing a helmet bearing several phrases, including "Kill yourself," according to the criminal complaint
Federal prosecutors said he had been planning the attack since January, when he began buying supplies and visiting sites around New York.

Arrabaca allegedly told law enforcement that he went to several other sites around the city bringing materials and considered attacking them. After months, he decided to attack the federal building near the courthouse.
A federal officer investigates the scene after an incendiary device went off outside 26 Federal Plaza in Lower Manhattan early on Monday in New York City. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
On Sunday, he made his way to Lower Manhattan with the weapons and other items used during the attack, prosecutors allege. He spent the night in a park and arrived at the building on Monday morning.
He told law enforcement he targeted a specific entrance because it was busy and employees were heading to work and members of the public were heading inside.
Arrabaca admitted that he was aware people could be hurt and was willing to accept the risk, said prosecutors, who described his actions as "calculated." He was also aware he could die.

Surveillance images included in the complaint show people standing just feet from the entrance when Arrabaca allegedly ignited the flammable liquid, while prosecutors say at least one victim suffered a gash to the back of the head after being struck by debris from the fire or explosion.

Defense lawyer Jennifer Brown said Arrabaca has mental health issues, and asked that he be placed in a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) mental health hospital for evaluation and treatment. Prosecutors noted that Arrabaca does not have a stable residence or employment and was living out of a car before the attack.

"The mental health issues that are quite likely the cause of the behavior, I seriously considered the alternatives proposed by Ms. Brown, but I had to reject them because I don’t think it’s sufficiently clear you would comply with treatment," Tarnofsky told Arrabaca.
Andrew Arrabaca, 43, allegedly fire several rounds from a pellet gun after setting the fire.  (Justice Department)

The federal building in Lower Manhattan has been the scene of protests against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the agency charged with enforcing the nation's immigration laws amid the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
One of two people hurt during Monday's incident was an immigrant who appeared at the building for a hearing, the FBI said.
A preliminary hearing is scheduled for Aug. 4. He faces a mandatory minimum of seven years in prison.
Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price and Michael Ruiz contributed to this report.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Singer D4vd shows no emotion as detective recounts gruesome discovery of teen's dismembered remains: report
summary: Gruesome testimony revealed maggots and flies in the Tesla trunk where prosecutors say D4vd left 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez's remains.
story: Rising recording artist David Burke, known as D4vd, is accused of murdering and dismembering a 14-year-old girl just two days before his first album dropped.

The California singer accused of grooming a 14-year-old girl only to murder her when she threatened to expose him and then dismembering her remains with a chainsaw appeared in front of a Los Angeles judge Tuesday for the first day of a preliminary hearing expected to clear the way for the case to go to trial.

David Burke, who performs under the name "D4vd," is accused of killing a teen girl named Celeste Rivas Hernandez, whose unrecognizable remains prosecutors say were found chopped up and decomposing in the trunk of his Tesla, abandoned 400 feet up the street from his home in Hollywood Hills.
Two of her fingers, which contained identifying tattoos, were never recovered.
Burke faces charges of murder, child sex abuse and unlawful mutilation of human remains.
RISING SINGER DISMEMBERED TEEN WHO THREATENED TO EXPOSE HIM IN KIDDIE POOL WITH CHAINSAW: DA
Singer D4vd was arrested in Los Angeles in the murder of a 14-year-old girl found in a Tesla trunk, police say. (Timothy Norris/Getty Images for Coachella)

Prior to the hearing, which is expected to take about three to five days, Celeste's parents, Jesus Rivas and Mercedes Martinez, were spotted entering the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office.
There were no cameras allowed in the courtroom Tuesday as prosecutors displayed gruesome images and shared brutal details with the court.

A Los Angeles homicide detective took the stand to discuss the grisly scene, with Celeste's parents opting to remain in the gallery when given a chance to leave before his testimony, according to FOX 11 Los Angeles.

Photographs, intimate notes and flowers are among the items left at a memorial for slain teen Celeste Rivas Hernandez, who was found dead in the trunk of a Tesla in a Hollywood tow yard on Sept. 25, 2025, in Lake Elsinore, Calif. (Gina Ferazzi/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)
"There were maggots," LAPD Det. Joshua Byers testified, according to the California Post. "There were flies. I don't know how to describe the other liquid matter."
Martinez looked like she might faint as a supporter leaned over to help her, according to the FOX LA report. Burke, shackled to a chair, reportedly showed no visible reaction.
SINGER D4VD ARRESTED AND HELD WITHOUT BAIL IN CASE TIED TO TEEN FOUND DEAD IN TESLA

The parents of Celeste Rivas, Jesus Rivas and Mercedes Martinez, arrive to the Hall of Justice in Los Angeles, Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Their daughter's alleged killer, D4vd, is in a pretrial hearing for the murder case. (Jef Steinberg/Splash for Fox News Digital)
Prosecutors allege that Burke first met Celeste when she was 11 and began molesting her in November 2023, when she was 13 and he was 18.
Los Angeles District Attorney Nathan Hochman told reporters outside the courthouse that a decision on whether to seek the death penalty has not yet been made.

Los Angeles District Attorney Nathan Hochman addresses the media outside the Foltz courthouse in Los Angeles July 21, 2026. Hip-hop star D4vd is facing a pretrial hearing for the murder of Celeste Rivas.  (Jeff Steinberg/Splash for Fox News Digital)
Prosecutors expect to call 10 witnesses, including members of the police department and coroner's office.

Burke and Celeste spent "a significant amount of time" together in 2024, when Burke allegedly flew the child to Las Vegas, London and Texas and introduced her to his family, prosecutors have alleged in court filings. In November of that year, however, they "broke up."

"[Text] messages reveal the victim's jealousy over defendant's relationships with other women, as defendant led her to believe they had a future together," prosecutors wrote. "She became extremely upset and threatened to disclose damaging information about her relationship with defendant to end his career and destroy his life."
SINGER D4VD PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO MURDER OF YOUNG GIRL ALLEGEDLY FOUND DISMEMBERED, DECOMPOSING IN HIS CAR

That was two days before his debut album dropped. Burke allegedly ordered Celeste an Uber and is accused of concocting a "plan to cover up the murder" that involved sending text messages to her phone asking where she was — allegedly after he'd already stabbed her to death.
A mugshot of D4vd, who is facing a first-degree murder charge in the death of a 14-year-old girl. (Los Angeles County District Attorney)

The morning after the murder, Burke sat for a radio interview about his forthcoming album, prosecutors have said previously.
During the interview on "The Zach Sang Show," he discussed "losing relationships" and how he could turn the losses into songs, including one named "Romantic Homicide."
